page: Vultr vbm-8c-64gb-amd is a dedicated bare metal server within the Bare Metal NVMe family, powered by an eight-core, sixteen-thread AMD EPYC 4345P processor operating at a base clock speed of 3.9 GHz. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this single-socket platform includes 64 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core, and bundles 3890 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage along with a single complimentary public IPv4 address. The server operates without virtualization overhead and contains no discrete graphics accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional single-threaded compute capability, propelled by the 3.9 GHz clock frequency and AMD Zen microarchitecture with AVX-512 vector support. The instance achieved top-tier rankings in both Geekbench single-core (score of 3291.0) and stress-ng single-core (score of 4645.0) assessments, complemented by top-decile throughput in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. In contrast, multi-core metrics reflect the physical eight-core topology, placing Geekbench multi-core (11684.0) and stress-ng multi-core (36127.68) performance firmly within the middle 50 percent of tested cloud hardware.

Memory subsystem testing reveals contrasting characteristics. While small cached reads achieve high throughput (2099.39 GB/sec) and the PassMark memory benchmark places the instance in the top tier, large uncached write operations showed reduced bandwidth (24.43 GB/sec), landing in the bottom quartile. CPU-based machine learning inference reflects this split: prompt processing and text generation for small models (135M parameters) reach upper-quartile speeds, but larger 7B model execution moderates to standard middle-tier rates.

Given its combination of high per-core clock rates, 3890 GB of direct-attached NVMe storage, and dedicated bare-metal isolation, the vbm-8c-64gb-amd delivers solid resource density without multi-tenant contention. It is technically appropriate for latency-sensitive single-threaded tasks, localized databases requiring high IOPS, build and compilation pipelines, and transactional web serving layers.
description: Vultr vbm-8c-64gb-amd is a dedicated bare metal server powered by an eight-core, sixteen-thread AMD EPYC 4345P processor clocked at 3.9 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 64 GB of memory and a bundled 3890 GB local NVMe SSD, this server provides dedicated, non-virtualized resources without discrete GPU hardware. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate top-tier single-core performance, evidenced by high Geekbench single-core and compression scores, while multi-threaded compute remains centered in the median tier due to the eight-core ceiling. Memory benchmarks demonstrate high cached read throughput alongside constrained large-block write bandwidth. The integrated high-capacity NVMe drive and strong per-core processing make this configuration suitable for localized relational databases, software build pipelines, static web serving, and single-thread bound transactional workloads.
